LESSON: OUR MARKET

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Social Environment
Topic 1.5: Our Market
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 9

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Our Market, part of Social Environment in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why do we have markets?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Our Market together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital Literacy: Interaction with digital technology as learners take photographs of things found in the market using adapted

digital devices.

Values:
Unity: Co-operation is enhanced as learners draw and colour different fruits and vegetables found in the market in groups.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social-economic issues: Skill of career awareness as learners draw and colour different fruits and vegetables found in the

market.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Mathematics Activities: Sorting and grouping as learners sort and group fruits and vegetables found in the market.

20

Suggested Learning Resources:

Approved Learning support materials, Local environment with appropriate environmental adaptations, Vegetables, Fruits,

theme based multi-purpose communication boards/ Photographs or picture cut outs made of heavy gauge material, with legible

and appropriate colour contrast on the market, adapted pencils and crayons with enhanced grip, hand stabilizers, pen/ pencils

grips, adapted digital devices with appropriate accessibility features and software, foot-boards, slates,

Related Service Providers:Physiotherapists, Occupational Therapists, Speech Therapists, Resource Persons, Learner Support

the learner should be able to;


a) identify roles of people

found in a market,


b) list food items found in a

market,


c) categorise food items

found in a market into

fruits and vegetables,


d) Appreciate activities that

are carried out in a

market.

• In purposive groups/ pairs or

individually, learners are

appropriately positioned/

seated and guided to observe

pictures of people found in a

market using appropriate

Assistive devices for

manipulation. Work surfaces/

tables should be at appropriate

heights.

learners are guided to share

market by the use of any

and/ Assistive technology for

support.

• Learners are appropriately

positioned/ seated and guided

to draw and colour/ trace/

learners are appropriately

positioned/ seated and guided

18

support. The working surfaces

should be at the appropriate

height for ease of

cards.

• In purposive groups or pairs,

learners are appropriately

positioned/ seated and guided

to use adapted learner digital

devices with appropriate

accessibility features and

software or picture cut outs of

food items found in a market

(mounted on heavy gauge

card
s) and make a portfolio.

Learners with manipulation

difficulties who may not make

the portfolio on their own

could be given physical

support under their instruction.

They could alternatively create

devices.

• Learners are appropriately

positioned/ seated and guided

to recite/ mime poems and

sing/ hum songs on food items

found in the market. Learners

who may not vocalize could

alternatively use text to speech

software/dance to the tune of

the songs rhythmically/ point

the words in the lyrics as

others recite or sing.
